name: PixGuard Scanner
author: pixguardio

sections.description:
PixGuard Scanner detects copyrighted and stock images on your WordPress site using a 9-stage AI detection pipeline. Avoid DMCA takedowns, copyright trolls, and expensive legal fees.

Features:

  • Scan any page on your site for copyrighted images
  • Media Library integration with one-click scanning
  • Auto-scan images on upload (optional)
  • Risk scores and severity ratings for every image
  • Dashboard with scan history and risk summary
  • Source attribution showing where images originate

How it works:

  1. Install the plugin and enter your PixGuard API key
  2. Scan pages or individual images from the WordPress admin
  3. Review risk scores and take action on flagged images

Detection capabilities:

  • Watermark detection (visible and invisible)
  • EXIF/metadata analysis (camera, software, copyright fields)
  • Perceptual hash matching against known stock databases
  • AI visual analysis for stock photo characteristics
  • Steganography detection
  • Source attribution via reverse image search

External Services

This plugin connects to the PixGuard API (https://api.pixguard.io) to analyze images for copyright risk. When you scan an image, its URL or file is sent to the PixGuard servers for processing. No images are stored on PixGuard servers after analysis.

This connection is required for the plugin to function. A free PixGuard account with an API key is needed.

  • Service website: https://pixguard.io
  • Privacy policy: https://pixguard.io/privacy
  • Terms of service: https://pixguard.io/terms
sections.installation:
1. Upload the pixguard-scanner folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu
  3. Go to PixGuard > Settings and enter your API key
  4. Get your API key at pixguard.io/dashboard/settings
sections.faq:
How much does it cost?

PixGuard uses a credit-based system. Each image scan costs 1 credit. Cached results (images scanned before) are free. New accounts get 100 free credits.

Does it work with Cloudflare?

Yes. The plugin sends image URLs to the PixGuard API for analysis. As long as your images are publicly accessible, it works with any CDN or security plugin.

Does it scan private/draft content?

The plugin scans via public URLs, so images must be accessible. For local development, use the Media Library scan which uploads images directly.
